fields.h1: Build a Bible Quiz That Shows the Verse Behind Each Answer
fields.hero_description: Build a Bible quiz for your group that scores each answer with its verse and saves results to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Bible Quiz on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A Bible quiz checks what a group remembers from a passage. Emergent builds the questions and the table that keeps the scores.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your passage

Name a book or a few chapters, and Emergent drafts questions on that text with wrong choices from the same story. Check each one against your Bible and change it by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
The chapter and verse after every answer

The results screen lists each question with the right answer and its reference, such as Jonah 1:17. A missed question becomes a verse to read that night instead of a lost point.
fields.feature_3:
Scores kept in a table your church owns

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the player and the date. Sort by question to see what the group missed, or by name to follow one person's season.
fields.feature_4:
Made for phones passed around a room

Players answer one question per screen with a progress bar on top, on a phone at youth night or a shared classroom tablet. Emergent sets no cap on how many people take it.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders for anyone who has not played

Set a deadline, and the app emails a reminder to each member who has not finished by then. The group leader can also get a Slack message listing the names still out that week.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code, free to start

Use your church's domain, included in Emergent and using credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository. The free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Groups Run a Bible Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
Team Acacia takes next month's pick on 52 points

Every Wednesday, 24 teens at Orchard Glen Church split into 4 teams of 6 and take a 10-question quiz on their phones. The app adds up each team's points out of 60 and puts the totals on the projector. Last week Team Acacia scored 52, ahead of Team Olive at 47, and chose next month's book.
fields.tab_content_2:
Six children open next Sunday on a 2-minute recap

After the lesson, the 18 children in grades 3 to 5 at Stillwater Bend Baptist take a 6-question quiz with 3 choices per question. Each child sees a score and the verse behind every answer. This week 12 of 18 scored 5 or 6. The other 6 open next Sunday on a 2-minute recap of the story.
fields.tab_content_3:
Seven readers get a Saturday reminder by email

The 31 adults in East Fennick Fellowship's reading group read Acts at 4 chapters a week. Every Monday, an 8-question check-in on that week's chapters opens. Anyone who has not taken it by Saturday gets an email reminder, and this week 7 of 31 got one before the group met on Sunday.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each section gets 20 different questions from a bank of 60

Two sections of seventh graders at Lantern Hill Christian Academy, 46 students in all, take a unit test on Exodus. The app draws 20 questions from a 60-question bank, and each section gets its own set. The 9 students who score under 12 of 20 join a Thursday study session.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Bible Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a Bible quiz that tests what your group read and shows which passages to go over again.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Use the translation your group reads
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Tie every question to a verse
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a single book or a run of chapters your group read this week, such as Ruth or Acts 1 to 4. A quiz on one passage shows what stuck from that reading. Put the passage in your prompt, and Emergent drafts questions on it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Word every question and answer the way the Bible your group carries words it, whether that is the King James Version or a modern one. Check each right answer in that translation before the quiz goes out, and name the translation on the first screen.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each question from a verse you can point to, and note the reference beside it. If you cannot find the verse in a minute, cut the question or rewrite it from the text. The reference then shows on the results screen.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Draw the wrong choices from people, places, and numbers in the same passage, and keep them close in length to the right one. Skip joke choices. A player should have to remember the story, not spot the odd one out.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Match the level to the age
fields.howto_step_5_des: For children under 10, use 3 choices and short words, with one idea per question. For teens and adults, use 4 choices and mix in questions on who said a line or where an event took place. Keep a kids' quiz to about 6 questions.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have one co-leader and one regular member take the quiz before the group does. Look for a question with two defensible answers or a reference that points to the wrong verse. Fix both, then send the link.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the quiz closes, sort the answers by question and open the next meeting with the 2 missed the most. Read each verse aloud, ask the question again, and put it back into a quiz a month later.

faq_plan.a: A Bible quiz is a set of scored questions about the people, events, and teaching in the Bible. It can cover one chapter or the whole Bible. A well-made one gives the chapter and verse behind each answer, which sends a player who misses straight back to the text.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a bible quiz?
faq_plan.a: Pick the passage and your group's translation, then draft questions you can check against the text. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the passage and your group in a prompt. Emergent builds the quiz and the table of answers, and a follow-up prompt adds the next chapter.

faq_plan.q: How do I write good Bible quiz questions and answers?
faq_plan.a: Write good Bible quiz questions and answers by asking what a careful reader of the passage would know: who spoke, where an event took place, or what happened next. Give each question one answer the verse supports. Avoid questions that turn on one translation's exact wording, since part of your group may read another.

faq_plan.q: How do I make Bible quiz questions for kids?
faq_plan.a: Write Bible quiz questions for kids about the one story from that day's lesson. Read the questions aloud for younger readers, and show the verse after each answer instead of a class ranking. If the story uses hard words such as covenant or parable, a short vocabulary quiz on those words can come first.

faq_plan.q: How many questions on a Bible quiz work best?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 8 to 12 questions for teens and adults and about 6 for young children. That covers a passage without turning a meeting into a test. A school unit test can run to 20, and the quiz on this page has 8.

faq_plan.q: Should a Bible quiz with answers show them after each question or at the end?
faq_plan.a: Show them at the end if you want a true score. When the answer appears after each question, a player can use one answer to work out the next. Put the player's choice beside the right one on the results screen. On Emergent, a follow-up prompt switches to instant feedback if your group prefers it.

faq_plan.q: How do I run a Bible quiz night for a church group?
faq_plan.a: Run it in teams of 4 to 6, with rounds of 10 questions on one book each, and show the team totals after every round. Open with a few funny survey questions about the group, such as the best potluck dish, to warm up the room before the scored rounds start.

faq_plan.q: Can a Bible quiz be scored by team instead of by person?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Let every member answer on their own phone and add the members' points into one team total. Keep the teams the same size, or compare averages instead of totals. Then a team of 5 is not behind before it starts. On Emergent, each answer still sits in the table under the player's name.

faq_plan.q: What Bible quiz questions work for adults who know the Bible well?
faq_plan.a: Questions on connections work best for them: which book a line comes from, who said it, or which two events share a chapter. Add one question on a book your group reads less often. Keep to questions whose answers you can cite: a debate then ends at the verse.

faq_plan.q: How do I ask my group for feedback on the Bible quiz questions?
faq_plan.a: Ask 2 or 3 short questions after the results screen: was it too easy, should the next one cover the same book, and would they come to a quiz night. A yes no questions survey keeps it under a minute, and the answers tell you whether to change the length or the level.

quiz.title: Bible Quiz: 8 Questions, Each With Its Verse
quiz.intro: Eight questions from Genesis to John, in the wording of the King James Version. Pick one answer per question; your score and the verse behind each answer show at the end.

questions.text: In Genesis 6, what kind of wood was Noah told to build the ark from?
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:14 gives the instruction to make an ark of gopher wood, with rooms made inside it.

source.quote: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark

questions.text: According to Genesis 7, how long was the rain upon the earth?
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:12 gives the span: forty days and forty nights of rain upon the earth.

source.quote: And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights

questions.text: In 1 Samuel 17, what did David sling at the Philistine?
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 17:49, David takes a stone from his bag, slings it, and strikes the Philistine in the forehead.

source.quote: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead

questions.text: According to Matthew 2, in which town was Jesus born?
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:1 names the town and places the birth in the days of Herod the king.

source.quote: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king

questions.text: In Jonah 1, what did the LORD prepare to swallow up Jonah?
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:17 says Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

source.quote: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights

questions.text: In John 6, how many barley loaves did the lad have?
questions.explanation: John 6:9 lists five barley loaves and two small fishes. Two is the number of fishes, not loaves.

source.quote: There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes

questions.text: In Exodus 31, on which mountain were the two tables of testimony given to Moses?
questions.explanation: Exodus 31:18 describes the two tables of testimony as tables of stone, given upon mount Sinai.

source.quote: when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone

questions.text: In Daniel 6, where was Daniel cast at the king's command?
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:16 says the king commanded, and Daniel was cast into the den of lions.

source.quote: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions
